title: No task waits silently: a step that stops moving is escalated once per stall
prompt:
Read `decide_with`, `Why`, `Escalation` and `Facts` (`current_observation`, `evidence_seq`, `dispatched`) in crates/spawn-cli/src/dispatch.rs; `order` and `heading` in crates/spawn-cli/src/dispatch/digest.rs and `decide_worker` in dispatch/worker.rs; `Work` (`blocked`, `in_flight`), `Turns`, `attempts`, `orders`, `delivered` and `news_items` in crates/spawn-cli/src/deliver.rs; `DELIVERY_TASKS` and `MISSION_NEWS` in crates/spawn-postgres/src/missions.rs and `DISPATCH_FACTS` in fleet.rs; `Integrator::mission`, `Mission::ready`, `Mission::landing`, `judge`, `halt` and `enforce_budget` in crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs; the fold of `task.*` and `mission.halted` records in crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql (`spawn_control_record`); docs/fleet-architecture.md §3 and §10.3; and the causality rule in docs/design.md (if it is not there yet, it is: no loop acts on another loop's progress inferred from timing, absence or the latest state; it acts only on a record that names what it covers, and every side effect has a recorded outcome that consumers check).

The problem. Work stalled silently five times in one day, and each time a human asking "check" found it: a conflict verdict with no way forward until the budget aborted the task; a failed delivery that blocked its own retry (a task assigned and never delivered); a stale judgement (an idle worker that never got its next task); a cancelled task's worker that kept working for 45 minutes; an owner push that halted a mission. Each has, or will get, a fix of its own (objectives 010-012, branch delivery-retry). The systemic gap is that nothing in Spawn notices when work stops moving. The supervisor hears only of events (`news_items`, the worker ladder): a stall is the absence of an event, so it produces no digest item, and the supervisor narrates "no action from me". Today a refused delivery reaches the supervisor only once its retries are spent (60 + 120 + 240 s), a worker silent in the middle of a turn never does, and a halted mission never does.

Required behaviour (the contract the gate checks). Spawn knows, for every open task, the step it waits on and since which record, and escalates a step that has not moved within its bound, once per stall.
1. Steps, derived from records only. Every open task is at exactly one step:
- `delivery`: assigned or sent back (`revise`), and its session's turn (the task the dispatcher delivers next for that session: a revision first, then the oldest new task, with no earlier open task of the session holding it, `Work::blocked`). Measured from the record that put it there (`task.assigned`, or the review that sent it back). A task waiting behind another task of its session is queued and never escalated itself: the task ahead of it is.
- `activity`: delivered, waiting for its worker's activity. Measured from the later of `task.delivered` and the session's latest fact: a record of the session that is not the Observer's nor storage's (`artifact.committed`, `merge.conflicted`), the facts `evidence_seq` counts. Any new fact moves the step. A worker idle at its prompt with no report collected is at this step too.
- `judgement`: reported (or, in a gated mission, accepted and waiting for the gate). Under review (`accept` = `review`): waiting for the supervisor, from `task.reported`. Gated: only the task the integrator judges next in its mission (`Mission::ready`'s order) is measured, from the later of its report and the mission's latest verdict that is not `stale`; the others are queued behind it. A `stale` verdict does not move the step; it is evidence.
- `landing`: `landing`, from its `task.gated` accepted record.
- `stop`: an ephemeral task closed (accepted without a gate, landed, cancelled) whose worker is still live, from the record that closed it. (Telling a resident of a cancel is objective 012's.)
- `halted`: a halted mission with open tasks, from its `mission.halted` record: one escalation per halt, about the mission, naming the reason and its open tasks.
A failed command is the evidence of the step it blocks (a delivery attempt, a switch-model Stop, a retire Stop, a resume), not a step of its own.
2. Bounds, in whole seconds, read by `spawn loop` from its environment, each with a default and a reason stated in docs/architecture.md (its environment table): `SPAWN_STALL_DELIVERY_SECS` (600: well past the first retry, 60 s, and a worker finishing a turn), `SPAWN_STALL_ACTIVITY_SECS` (900: a long build or test run writes nothing for minutes), `SPAWN_STALL_REVIEW_SECS` (1800), `SPAWN_STALL_GATE_SECS` (3600: the gate's own wall clock is 45 min), `SPAWN_STALL_LANDING_SECS` (600), `SPAWN_STALL_STOP_SECS` (300), `SPAWN_STALL_HALTED_SECS` (0: a halt waits for a human from the start). A value that is not a non-negative integer is a warning on the loop's log and the default.
3. The escalation. One new digest item kind, `Why::Stalled`, with the heading `stalled`. Why a new kind when objective 009 avoided one: a parallel worker's report is a report and fits `Report`; a stall is no event at all, says something no existing item says (this task's step has not moved for this long, here is why), and asks the supervisor for a different decision (check, cancel, reassign, resume). One kind with the step in the item, not one kind per step. Its escalation id is `stall-<task>-<step>-<n>` (so its tag is `<session> stall-<task>-<step>-<n>`), where `<n>` names the record the step is measured from: the control record's id, or, for `activity`, the `session_seq` of the latest fact (the delivery record's id when no fact came after it). For `halted` the item is about session `missions` with id `stall-mission-<mission>-halted-<record>`. The item is one line of the digest, as every item is, and names: `task #<id>`; the step word; how long it has stood still; the evidence (the record it is measured from and its age, the latest judgement's state and whether it covers the latest fact, each failed command with its idempotency key and error, the latest stale verdict's reason); and what Spawn already tried (every attempt of the delivery with its key and outcome, a retry still due, or due and held, and why it is held; a nudge, a resume, the idle or report item already sent).
- Once per stall: the tag is the existing `told` mechanism, so a stall is escalated once, and again only after its step moved and stalled anew (a new record, so a new `<n>`). A retry that fails again, a stale verdict, a nudge or a judgement does not move a step.
- A delivery that failed for good is already escalated by `DeliveryFailed`; that is its stall's escalation, and no stall item is sent for a delivery whose attempts are given up.
- Without a supervisor, stall items stay pending in the attention queue like every other item.
4. Recoveries. The stall layer itself takes no action; it adds digest items only. The safe recoveries are the ones Spawn already has, on their own schedules, and they come first because every default bound is longer than their first attempt: the dispatcher's delivery retries (and the not-ready retry of branch delivery-retry once it is on main); the resume of a lost ephemeral worker and the liveness rule for residents; the integrator judging a `stale` report again on its next pass; the retire Stop of a closed ephemeral worker. A stall is escalated once its bound has passed, whatever recovery is still to come, and the item names it (due, or due and held, with why). Not allowed, because each needs a decision or may do harm: typing into a worker (no nudge into a busy turn, no line to refresh a judgement), delivering a task again after an attempt that may have typed it, cancelling or reassigning, resuming a halted mission, stopping a resident, extending a budget.
5. Causality. Stalls are computed in the dispatcher's step from the log: task rows and the control records that name the task, the session's facts by `session_seq`, and commands with their recorded outcomes. Ages use one clock, the database's (`spawn_now_ms()` against `recorded_at_ms`, `created_at_ms` and `finished_at_ms`), never the loop host's clock against a database time. No step is inferred from another loop's timing or absence ("the integrator has not run lately"): it is measured from the record that started it, and the item names that record. The dispatcher stays stateless: a restarted loop computes the same stalls and the same tags.
6. Out of scope: the RSI and Missions pages (showing a stalled task as stalled there is a later objective), and any new action on a stalled task.
State the rule in docs/fleet-architecture.md §3 (the escalations the dispatcher makes, with the steps and bounds), in the module comments of dispatch.rs and deliver.rs (or of a new module such as dispatch/stall.rs), and in docs/architecture.md (the variables). Add unit tests:
- each step derived from task rows, records and facts;
- a task queued behind another of its session, and a gated task behind the mission's next one, are not escalated;
- the bound's edges (one second before and at the bound);
- a new fact changes the `activity` tag, and a failed retry does not change the `delivery` tag;
- a delivery given up (`DeliveryFailed`) gets no stall item;
- the item's line names the task, the step, the failed attempts' keys and errors, and the judgement's state;
- a halted mission is escalated once per `mission.halted` record;
- in crates/spawn-postgres/tests/, the query that feeds this returns the step's record and its age on the database's clock.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/013.sh (read it). A real `spawn loop` runs a supervisor and four residents on a fake engine, with no model judge, in one mission under review. The loop's environment sets `SPAWN_STALL_DELIVERY_SECS=90` and `SPAWN_STALL_ACTIVITY_SECS=30`, and every other bound to 600. The harness reviews like a supervisor, accepting each healthy report as soon as it is collected, and types a line into the supervisor now and then (`ping_supervisor`, as in 006.sh, because objective 011 may not be solved on your base). Two stalls are injected from outside Spawn:
- `stuck`: a tmux wrapper refuses every paste-buffer and send-keys into the stuck resident's pane, so its task's delivery never lands. The dispatcher's retry, 60 s later, fails the same way, or is held while that worker has no current judgement.
- `quiet`: its engine takes the task, opens the turn and goes silent.
Beside them, `busy` works through a 60 s turn with a tool call every 0.5 s, and `quick` takes 2 s; both report and are accepted. An escalation is a digest that `spawn-dispatch` delivered to session_supervisor (an input command that succeeded) carrying the tag `<session> stall-<task>-<step>-<n>`. Checked:
- (1) the stuck task gets exactly one escalation, step `delivery`, between 90 s and 120 s after its `task.assigned`. Its line names `task #<id>`, `delivery`, `deliver-<id>-0`, that attempt's error (the wrapper's `refused by the scenario`), and the key of every other attempt that had failed by then. Later failed retries add none.
- (2) the quiet task gets exactly one escalation, step `activity`, between 30 s and 60 s after its session's latest fact. Its line names `task #<id>`, `activity`, that fact's event name and the state of the session's latest judgement.
- (3) the quiet worker then makes one tool call and goes silent again. That stall gets exactly one escalation of its own, with a new tag, at least 30 s after the new fact, and the first is not sent again.
- (4) the healthy tasks get no stall tag at all, and no stall tag names anything but the two stalled tasks, over a window of at least 240 s.
On c98c1e8 it fails at (1) ("no escalation of task #1 stuck at its delivery"). It exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when an assertion fails, 2 on a harness failure.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base (do not delete, rename, ignore or disable tests), any lint relaxation ([lints] tables, clippy.toml, a new crate-level #![allow]/#![expect], a removed #![warn]/#![deny]) and any build-time code (build.rs, .cargo/, a `build =` key in a Cargo.toml). The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host: a new crate builds only if it is already in ~/.cargo/registry. Keep every existing check green (clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios, the web build) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
